div.head: I Cn 26
div.ab: Bisceopas syndan bydelas ⁊ Godes lage lareowas, ⁊ hi sceolon bodian ⁊ bysnian georne godcunde þearfe, gyme se ðe wylle.
Bisceopas syndon bydelas ⁊ Godes larðeowas, ⁊ hy scylan bodian ⁊ bisnian georne godcunde ðéarfe, gyme se ðe wylle.
Biscopas syndon bydalas ⁊ Godes lage lareowæs, ⁊ hig sceolan bodian ⁊ bysnian georne godcunde þearfe, gyme se þe wylle.
Episcopi sunt precones et doctores legis Dei; qui predicationibus et exemplis Dei debent misteria declarare, curet qui uelit;
Episcopi sunt precones Dei et diuine legis doctores; hii debent cum summa diligencia predicare et exemplificare spirituale proficuum, obseruet qui uelit.
Bisceopas syndon bydelas ⁊ Godes larðeowas ⁊ hy scylan bodian ⁊ bisnian georne godcunde ðéarfe, gyme se ðe wylle.
Bisceopas syndan bydelas and Godes lage lareowas, and hi sceolon bodian and bysnian georne godcunde þearfe, gyme se ðe wylle.
Die Bischöfe sind die Herolde und Lehrer des Gottesgesetzes (Gottes Lehrer B) und sie sollen künden und durch Beispiel ernstlich darlegen, was geistlich noth thut; achte [dessen], wer will.
Bishops are heralds and teachers of God's law (God's teachers, B), and they must preach and eagerly show by example what is spiritually needful; let him heed it who will.
The bishops are God's heralds and teachers, and they shall proclaim and zealously give example of our duty towards God—let him who will take heed.
Bishops are messengers and teachers of God’s law, and they are to diligently proclaim and embody our spiritual duty, heed them who will.

note.quote: it was also combined with nearby Polity passages to supply the conclusion to the ecclesiastical part of Cnut's code, I Cn 26 – 26:4

div.note: B's ‘larðeowas’ is Middle English.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 305, October 2026 (MS Cons)

note.seg: Diesen Satz und 26, 4 benutzt Grið 19f.; 26—26, 4 Polity ed. Thorpe 425. Verwandtes s. II Cn 84, 4, wie denn die Epiloge zu beiden Gesetzteilen einander ähneln; Cn 1020, 8; Hom. n. Wulfstan 79f., erste Zeile ebd. 176. 177.—Vgl. Gl Bischof 8a

This sentence and 26, 4 are used by Grið 19f.; 26—26, 4 by Polity ed. Thorpe 425. For related matter see II Cn 84, 4, just as the epilogues to the two parts of the law resemble each other; Cn 1020, 8; Hom. n. Wulfstan 79f., first line ibid. 176. 177.—Cf. Gl Bischof 8a
Ähnlich nennt Ælfric Pastor. (ed. Thorpe Anc. laws 452) u. Homil. (II 74. 536. I 36) die Priester ‘Lehrer, Führer’, den Bischof ‘Hirt gegen den Wolf’ d. i. den Teufel; s. d. Gl 5

Similarly Ælfric, Pastor. (ed. Thorpe Anc. laws 452) and Homil. (II 74. 536. I 36), calls the priests ‘teachers, leaders’, and the bishop ‘shepherd against the wolf’, i.e. the devil; see that word in Gl 5
Das Folgende bis 26, 4 wiederholt Polity 6 (ed. Anc. laws 425).—Gyme seþe wille auch o. 1b D
What follows up to 26, 4 is repeated by Polity 6 (ed. Anc. laws 425).—Gyme seþe wille also above 1b D
With caps. 26–26, 4, cf. Insts. of Polity, 6, ed. Thorpe, Anc. Laws, ii. p. 310.
Cf. II Cn. 84, 4; Ælfric, Homilies, ed. Thorpe, ii. p. 74.
